Article Title: LeT conspiracy case: NIA attaches Srinagar property used to shelter 2 Pakistani terrorists

NEW DELHI: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) on Monday attached a residential property in Srinagar Jammu and Kashmir , belonging to an accused in a case linked to a cross-border terrorist conspiracy involving the proscribed Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) outfit.The property, owned by Ghulam Mohammad Mir alias Mama Gas, is located in Danihama village in Srinagar’s Hazratbal area. The NIA attached it under Section 25 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.According to the anti-terror agency, its investigation established a direct link between the property and the terrorist conspiracy.“The premises were used for harbouring Pakistani terrorists and concealing incriminating material connected with the terror network. Investigation exposed a network of local Over Ground Workers (OGWs) working in coordination with LeT handlers to facilitate the infiltration, movement, shelter and logistical support of Pakistani terrorists for carrying out attacks against government establishments, security forces and civilians,” the statement read.The NIA also revealed that a search conducted at Mir’s residence on April 6 led to the detection of two Pakistani terrorists, identified as Abu Huraira and Khubaib, who were associated with the LeT.An explosive-like substance, digital devices and other incriminating material were also recovered and seized from the premises.The investigation further indicated that “the accused had knowingly provided his residential premises as a haven for the terrorists and had allowed the property to be used for facilitating their activities,” the agency noted.The NIA is continuing its probe to identify and expose the wider terror-support network, including other OGWs, facilitators and individuals linked to the Pakistan-based handlers.The case was initially registered at Zakoora Police Station in Srinagar on March 31, 2026, before being taken over and re-registered by the NIA.
Article Summary: The property, owned by Ghulam Mohammad Mir alias Mama Gas, is located in Danihama village in Srinagar’s Hazratbal area. The NIA attached it under Section 25 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.

Article Title: 'Anyone can join Shiv ki Baraat': Rahul Gandhi likens CEC protest to Lord Shiva's Tandav; BJP hits back
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi, Shivaraj Singh Chouhan

BJP attacks Congress over Lord Shiva reference

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Monday likened the ongoing protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar to “Lord Shiva’s Tandav”, saying the movement did not require a fixed plan and that anyone willing to join the fight to protect the Constitution was welcome.The remarks drew a sharp response from Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, who accused the Congress of having no connection with the country’s traditions and faith. “They do not even have the right to invoke the name of Lord Shiva,” he said.Speaking at a press conference at the All India Congress Committee (AICC) headquarters ahead of the INDIA bloc’s planned march to the Supreme Court, Gandhi said the protest would continue in different forms, depending on the circumstances.“My sister tells me that we should make a plan. So I told my sister, 'You are not understanding the point. This is Tandav. This is Lord Shiva’s dance. There is no planning in this. Today we are going to the Supreme Court; tomorrow it will be something else. What do you think? Did we make a plan at Akashvani Bhavan?“The plan was that we would go by bus, sit there, and get arrested. The police wouldn't let us go. So we changed the plan.Did the result come from the plan, or did it come from the non-plan? There is no need for any plan. This dance is ongoing. This is Lord Shiva’s dance going on. In this, anyone can join Shiva's procession (Shiv ki Baraat). Anyone who wants to join, can come,” he said.Gandhi said the demonstrations were aimed at questioning the conduct of the Election Commission and demanding Kumar’s resignation. He claimed that people across the country were raising questions about the chief election commissioner and warned that the agitation would continue.“Why is all this happening? Because we are only asking the question raised by two Election Commissioners: why is Gyanesh Kumar not resigning? These days, we are receiving information from everywhere. Gyanesh Kumar, we know your situation. We know you are unable to sleep at night, and do not worry, we will not spare you. I am telling you directly that you will not escape as Election Commissioner because of what is happening. Lakhs of people are questioning you and your conduct, and they will not stop,” he said.The Congress leader also alleged that questions were being raised within security agencies over the treatment of protesters compared with members of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS)."Questions are being raised within the police about why they are being asked to stop the youth while RSS members are being allowed to roam freely. These questions are being raised within the Home Ministry, Delhi Police, CRPF and ITBP,” he said.Gandhi urged people from all political parties to join the INDIA bloc’s march at 1.30 pm from Barakhamba Junction in Connaught Place, describing it as a movement to protect the Constitution. He also appealed to those unable to participate directly to express solidarity when the delegation reached the Supreme Court to file its petition."India is marching; join us today at 1.30 PM at Barakhamba Junction in Connaught Place. If you want to protect the Constitution, anyone from any party can join...If you cannot join us directly for any reason, show your solidarity when we will be in front of the Supreme Court filing the petition,” he said.Responding to Gandhi’s remarks, Chouhan accused the Congress of invoking religious symbolism despite, according to him, being disconnected from India’s cultural traditions."Look, I have said this before as well: they have nothing to do with the country’s values, traditions or faith. They do not even have the right to invoke the name of Lord Shiva," Chouhan said.The Union minister also dismissed the Opposition’s protests as an expression of frustration over repeated electoral defeats and accused the Congress of blaming constitutional institutions for its political setbacks."The reason for Congress's defeat is not the Election Commission; the reason for Congress's defeat is Congress's own idea-less leadership. What is the current state of the Congress? There is infighting in Uttar Pradesh. In Punjab, they have had to change the state president. In different places, there are conflicts over leadership. In Karnataka, sometimes it's Siddaramaiah, sometimes it's D.K. Shivakumar. In Telangana, there is internal conflict.Chouhan further accused the Congress of undermining constitutional institutions and cited its record of dismissing elected governments."What will they talk about the Constitution? They have sinned by changing elected governments more than 90 times," he said.The INDIA bloc’s planned march comes amid Opposition allegations of electoral irregularities and demands for Kumar’s resignation. The delegation intends to approach the Supreme Court with a petition raising concerns over the Election Commission and the conduct of elections.Security was tightened across central Delhi ahead of the march, with police barricades and deployments of Delhi Police, the Rapid Action Force and the Central Reserve Police Force. Entry and exit at several metro stations were also scheduled to remain closed until 4 pm for security reasons.
Article Summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi likens ongoing protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar to "Lord Shiva's Tandav" Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan accused the Congress of having no connection with the country's traditions and faith. Gandhi urged people from all political parties to join the march at 1.30 pm from Barakhamba Junction in Connaught Place.

Article Title: North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles towards S Korea, Seoul urges Pyongyang to stop ‘UN violations’
Article Text:
North Korea fires missiles towards sea, escalating tensions on Korean Peninsula (Reuters image)

North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles towards its eastern waters on Monday, South Korea’s military said, as Pyongyang continued its weapons testing amid heightened tensions and a prolonged freeze in diplomatic engagement.South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said the missiles were launched from an area near the North Korean capital, Pyongyang. Japan’s Defence Ministry detected at least two missiles and assessed that they had landed in waters outside the country’s exclusive economic zone.South Korea’s presidential office condemned the repeated launches, saying they violated United Nations Security Council resolutions and urging Pyongyang to stop such activities immediately.The latest launches came days after South Korea flight-tested its first domestically developed hypersonic weapon on Friday. Designed to travel at least five times the speed of sound and evade missile defence systems, the weapon was described by President Lee Jae Myung as an important step towards strengthening the country’s conventional defence capabilities.North Korea has intensified its weapons development as leader Kim Jong Un seeks to expand the country’s arsenal of nuclear-capable systems.On October 3, Pyongyang conducted a test of what it described as a hypersonic intermediate-range missile designed to penetrate missile defence systems in South Korea and Japan.The country has also carried out missile tests and live-fire drills and commissioned a new warship, underscoring Kim’s push to strengthen its military capabilities despite repeated US and South Korean offers to resume diplomatic engagement.Tensions on the Korean Peninsula have also been aggravated by a series of land mine explosions near the heavily militarised inter-Korean border last month that injured three South Korean soldiers. South Korea’s military and the US-led United Nations Command concluded that the blasts were caused by mines planted by North Korea. Pyongyang has denied responsibility and dismissed Seoul’s demands for an apology.Kim has halted diplomatic engagement and cooperation with South Korea in recent years, describing the neighbouring country as a permanent enemy. Nuclear negotiations with Washington have also remained stalled since 2019, when talks broke down during US President Donald Trump’s first term.Kim has so far rejected Trump’s overtures to revive dialogue. Pyongyang has demanded that Washington abandon what it calls its “hostile” policy and drop denuclearisation demands as a precondition for negotiations.The impasse has complicated Lee’s efforts to pursue engagement with North Korea. While advocating dialogue and adopting a more conciliatory tone, the South Korean president has also called for stronger conventional defence capabilities and reduced reliance on the United States.Washington unilaterally scaled back a major military exercise with South Korea in August, with Trump citing his “very good relationship” with Kim.
Article Summary: South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said the missiles were launched from an area near the North Korean capital, Pyongyang. Japan's Defence Ministry detected at least two missiles and assessed that they had landed in waters outside the country's exclusive economic zone. The latest launches came days after South Korea flight-tested its first domestically developed hypersonic weapon.

Article Title: 'Keep getting messages': Rahul Gandhi's big claim, and a message for CEC Gyanesh Kumar

NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Monday levelled serious allegations against chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the Narendra Modi-led Centre, claiming that around 200 government officials were in touch with the opposition and sharing information, including officials from the Enforcement Directorate (ED), Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) and the ministry of external affairs.Speaking at a press conference ahead of the INDIA bloc's planned march to the Supreme Court , Rahul said, "I want to tell Narendra Modi that 200 officials of your government are in touch with us and informing us, including those in the ED, CBI, foreign ministry..."Stepping up his attack on the poll body chief, Rahul claimed Kumar was having "sleepless nights" amid the opposition's campaign against alleged electoral irregularities.Responding to a reporter's question on whether he had communicated with the CEC, Rahul claimed that he had been "getting messages".When asked if he had a message for Gyanesh Kumar, Rahul said, "You have done a crime, and you are not the main criminal. You made a mistake and you are not the mind behind the mistake. We are after the people who are behind what you did. It is very easy for you, resign and get out of the way. We know that you have been forced by the Prime Minister, Amit Shah, Ajit Doval," Rahul Gandhi saidThe former Congress president also questioned why Kumar had not resigned, claiming that the opposition was receiving information from several sources."Why is all this happening? Because we are only asking the question raised by two Election Commissioners: why is Gyanesh Kumar not resigning? These days, we are receiving information from everywhere. Gyanesh Kumar, we know your situation. We know you are unable to sleep at night, and do not worry, we will not spare you. I am telling you directly that you will not escape as Election Commissioner because of what is happening. "Rahul also accused the Centre of turning Delhi into a fortress to protect the CEC, as INDIA bloc leaders prepared to march towards the Supreme Court to demand Kumar's removal over alleged "vote chori" and concerns surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.He said a public movement against alleged electoral irregularities had been under way in Delhi for the past four to five days, with protesters demanding Kumar's removal."Since last 4-5 days, public movement is on in Delhi against 'vote chori', seeking CEC removal," the Raebareli MP said.Referring to the police action during the October 10 protests, Rahul alleged that authorities were preventing people from reaching the national capital by stopping trains and buses and forcing passengers to get off."People are being stopped from reaching Delhi. Trains and buses are being stopped, and people are being made to get off. Delhi has been turned into a fortress, with 20,000 to 30,000 police personnel deployed everywhere. Now, think about how powerful this is. But our strategy is different," the former Congress chief said.Questioning the security arrangements, Rahul accused the government of making a "grave mistake" by protecting Kumar. He argued that the heavy police deployment would only help the opposition draw attention to its allegations against the CEC and the Centre."We want 20,000 to 30,000 police personnel deployed on the streets. The government is committing a grave mistake, because we want to show the country that Modi ji wants to ensure the security of Gyanesh Kumar... The more he is protected, the more we will ultimately reach his controller... We are receiving reports that police personnel are distressed because they are being ordered to beat up young people, while instructions are being issued to give RSS members a free hand. "Rahul further claimed that some police personnel supported the opposition's campaign and wanted it to continue."I am happy to tell you that 50% of the police personnel, and I am counting them, are telling us that what you are doing is right and that we should continue..."He also alleged that security personnel and ordinary citizens were increasingly opposed to the government's handling of the protests."Police, ITBP, CRPF, the people of India are on one side and Narendra Modi, Amit Shah, Ajit Doval, Gyanesh Kumar, and 4-5 members of the Election Commission who are facilitating 'vote chori' and hijacking the country are on the other side. We are increasing this divide..."Rahul said the opposition's resistance had been building for years and was now taking a more concrete form."There was resistance from 12 years but it is getting crystallised now," he said.He also announced that INDIA bloc leaders would approach the Supreme Court on Monday with a petition against the CEC over alleged "vote chori".The press conference came ahead of the INDIA bloc's planned march to the Supreme Court, with opposition leaders seeking Kumar's removal amid mounting criticism of the SIR exercise.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi claims 200 government officials are in touch with the opposition and sharing information. He says Gyanesh Kumar is having "sleepless nights" amid the opposition's campaign against alleged electoral irregularities. Rahul also accuses the Centre of turning Delhi into a fortress to protect the CEC.

Article Title: 'Your confidence is most vital': Supreme Court to Kapil Sibal after his 'no faith' remark
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Sunday said its purpose was to instill faith of the people in the system and addressed Kapil Sibal 's "no faith" remark, saying his "confidence is most vital" for the top court's "fight against injustice".“Our purpose is to instill faith of the people in the system and in that process your (Sibal’s) confidence is most vital for our fight against injustice,” the bench said.The Supreme Court on Sunday directed authorities to prevent illegal detention of people participating in peaceful gatherings amid the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests in Delhi. It also asked the Centre to ensure that metro services operate normally and internet access remains uninterrupted, subject to law and order requirements.Sibal welcomed the court's order in connection with the restrictions imposed in Delhi amid protests, saying it restores faith in the country's justice system.“We are deeply grateful to the Supreme Court for having passed an order that restores faith among professionals in the system of justice in this country,” Sibal said.A bench comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice to the Centre while hearing a petition seeking contempt proceedings over alleged violations of the court's earlier order against a "complete prohibition" on metro and train services in the national capital during the protests.The CJP and several student organisations had called for demonstrations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission.The authorities prevented a planned mass mobilisation at Jantar Mantar on Saturday following a major security clampdown. More than 7,000 protesters were detained, including CJP leader Abhijit Dipke, several opposition leaders and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee.During the special hearing, the bench asked Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to ensure that Delhi Metro operates according to its regular schedule and that internet services are not disrupted, subject to law and order requirements.The court also directed authorities to ensure that lawyers, journalists and others are not prevented from carrying out their professional duties."Internet facilities shall remain undisturbed, as per law....When we are saying internet facilities shall remain undisturbed, we are not taking away the powers under the Information Technology Act."There shall not be illegal detention, save and except by procedure established by law, particularly with regard to assemblage of people beyond the area within which it's imposed," the bench said.The Supreme Court also directed authorities to remove a notice board outside its premises announcing the imposition of Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which empowers authorities to restrict assemblies in certain circumstances."We have been informed that a notice board stating imposition of Section 163 BNSS in and around the vicinity of the Supreme Court has been put up."We direct the authority concerned to take down this board, if not already done, so that citizens as well as lawyers can have access to justice," the bench ordered.During the hearing, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) MP Manoj Jha, alleged that police were detaining people travelling on trains and those found outside the four-kilometre radius of Jantar Mantar, where prohibitory orders were in force.Sibal also told the court that 45 metro stations had remained closed to passenger entry and exit despite the Supreme Court's October 9 order.The petition sought contempt proceedings against the authorities over the alleged failure to comply with the court's directions on maintaining access to public transport during the protests.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Sunday directed authorities to prevent illegal detention of people participating in peaceful gatherings amid the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests in Delhi. It also asked the Centre to ensure that metro services operate normally and internet access remains uninterrupted, subject to law and order requirements.

Article Title: Delhi protests: SC on Tuesday to hear pleas on attacks on protesters, lawyers
Article Text:
CJP protesters detained during a demonstration at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi

‘Private hooligans are not being stopped’: Senior advocate seeks action

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday agreed to hear two separate pleas on Tuesday concerning the October 10 and 11 protests in Delhi, including allegations of attacks on lawyers and protesters and disruptions to the functioning of courts.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mahadevan said it would not allow the court to become a political battleground while agreeing to list a plea seeking action against alleged hooligans accused of attacking lawyers and protesters.Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan mentioned a plea seeking action against alleged hooligans who, he said, were attacking lawyers, young people and other protesters without facing police action.He also raised concerns over videos purportedly showing the alleged attackers recording their actions and proudly displaying them.“Private hooligans are not being stopped. They are making videos and proudly proclaiming what they have done. I am shocked. I’ve never seen a senior advocate being dragged on the streets. At some point, the Bench will have to come to the rescue of the Bar and young children,” Sankaranarayanan said.Referring to restrictions imposed under Section 163, he urged the court to ask the police to exercise restraint.“At a time when our senior advocates are being dragged through the streets, at such times I must urge the Court to convey to the police to exercise restraint,” he said.Separately, the SCBA mentioned its plea seeking directions to ensure that lawyers can move freely and court proceedings are not disrupted during protests.SCBA president and senior advocate Pradeep Rai said political parties should not interfere with lawyers’ work or affect the functioning of courts.CJI Surya Kant said he had already appealed to the authorities to ensure there was no impediment to court functioning or the movement of lawyers amid the restrictions imposed during the protests.The matters are now scheduled to be heard on Tuesday.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Monday agreed to hear two separate pleas on Tuesday concerning the October 10 and 11 protests in Delhi. The pleas include allegations of attacks on lawyers and protesters and disruptions to the functioning of courts. A bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mahadevan said it would not allow the court to become a political battleground.

NEW DELHI: A brief stir broke out at an official government function attended by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Chennai on Sunday after some people displayed placards projecting Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay as the “next PM”.The incident took place at the IIT Madras campus, where PM Modi was addressing a gathering after inaugurating and laying the foundation stone for projects worth around Rs 13,000 crore across Tamil Nadu.CM Vijay was also present at the event.During his speech, P Modi mentioned Vijay's name, prompting a group of people, apparently supporters of the chief minister, to whistle and display handwritten placards bearing Vijay's photographs and slogans, including “Next PM Vijay 2029”, according to news agency PTI.Police personnel deployed at the venue intervened and instructed the individuals to sit down and lower their placards.Although they complied initially, they continued displaying the placards after the police turned away, gesturing towards video cameras.The incident occurred during PM Modi's first visit to Tamil Nadu since the April Assembly elections, which brought Vijay's TVK to power.The prime minister and the chief minister shared the stage during the inauguration of several infrastructure projects.They also jointly flagged off a new Chennai Metro service and travelled on the train.PM Modi inaugurated the Poonamallee-Vadapalani stretch of Phase II of the Chennai Metro Rail Project, built at a cost of around Rs 4,900 crore. The new stretch covers approximately 15 km and has 11 elevated stations.The two leaders also jointly inaugurated other scheduled projects during the visit. Vijay received PM Modi on his arrival in Chennai and saw him off before his departure for Delhi.In his address, PM Modi said his commitment to Tamil Nadu's development would remain unchanged despite changes in government."Governments may change, but my resolve for Tamil Nadu's development, serving its people remains steadfast. With this determination to serve people, together with CM Vijay, we are taking forward the development of the state," he said.PM Modi also highlighted cooperative federalism, saying that the country's development depended on the progress of its states. He recalled his experience of working with several Tamil Nadu chief ministers during his political career.Vijay, meanwhile, said cooperation between the Union and state governments was essential to ensure that people benefited from development initiatives."When the union and state governments work together, its benefit should directly reflect in the lives of the people, and that is our approach," he said.The chief minister also sought the release of Rs 5,110 crore in outstanding central funds under the Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan scheme without conditions. He called for steps to make Tamil the principal language of the Madras High Court.Vijay also urged the Centre to approve Phase III of the Chennai Metro project, reconsider metro proposals for Coimbatore and Madurai, and consider an inter-state metro line linking Hosur in Tamil Nadu with Bommasandra near Bengaluru. He further sought high-speed rail corridors between Chennai and Kanyakumari and Chennai and Coimbatore.During the visit, PM Modi praised Tamil language and culture and referred to the ancient Tamil classic Thirukkural, describing it as a guide for life.He recalled gifting a Russian edition of the work to Russian President Vladimir Putin and cited its teachings on learning and putting knowledge into practice.PM Modi also paid tribute to national poet Mahakavi Bharati and referred to the continuing relevance of the poet's verse Achamillai, meaning “there is no fear”.The prime minister also inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for highway projects, Amrit railway stations, port-related initiatives and the Group II/III Lube Oil Base Stocks project at the Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited refinery in Manali.The visit included meetings and joint public appearances between PM Modi and Vijay as the two governments highlighted their cooperation on infrastructure and Tamil Nadu's development.
Article Summary: PM Modi vows to work with Vijay for Tamil Nadu's development. Incident occurred during PM Modi's first visit to Tamil Nadu since the April Assembly elections, which brought Vijay's TVK to power. Police personnel deployed at the venue intervened and instructed the individuals to sit down and lower their placards.

Article Title: HC questions Assam government on woman sent to Bangladesh
Article Text:
Not only Mumtaz, another woman also 'missing' after B'desh expulsion

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Gauhati high court has intensified scrutiny of circumstances in which Nagaon's Mumtaz Begum was sent to Bangladesh, warning Assam govt that it would presume a Foreigners' Tribunal's May 30 opinion declaring her a foreigner would be considered "not ready" if the state fails to establish when it was finalised.In its latest order on Oct 7, the high court recorded MEA's submission that an inquiry into Mumtaz's whereabouts was ongoing and that it needed more time.TOI had reported that Bangladesh's home ministry began searching for Mumtaz after this newspaper contacted authorities in Dhaka in the last week of Sept.The Gauhati high court, in its Oct 7 order, said, "The court shall presume that the opinion...was not made ready within the appropriate time, i.e., prior to the taking into custody" of Mumtaz.The court had ordered an inquiry on Sept 3 and directed MEA to trace Mumtaz and facilitate her return, observing that she was sent to Bangladesh without a "reasonable opportunity" to challenge the tribunal's opinion.The court had previously set aside an earlier opinion declaring her a foreigner and ordered fresh consideration of her case.Her son, Momruz Ali, had on Oct 7 disputed Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma's claim that she was safe and in regular contact with him and had told TOI that the family had no idea where she was and that the family was "breaking" under the strain of the search.The case dates back to April, when Gauhati HC set aside an earlier Foreigners' Tribunal opinion declaring Mumtaz a foreigner and remanded the matter for fresh consideration. She appeared before the tribunal again on May 30, the date borne by the fresh opinion, and was taken into custody.The central question now before the court is whether that opinion had actually been made ready before officials acted on it.According to the chronology recorded in court proceedings, Mumtaz was subsequently moved through holding facilities in Assam and handed over to BSF on June 13.BSF told the court she was "sent back to Bangladesh" in the early hours of June 14, from the Kalaincherra area of Cachar. Her whereabouts have remained unknown to her family since she was sent across the border, according to her son.Mumtaz is not the only woman from Nagaon reported missing after being sent across the border. Another woman, Jahanara Begum, whose case is ongoing in HC, has also gone missing under similar circumstances.The high court heard her case together with that of Mumtaz Begum.
Article Summary: Gauhati high court has intensified scrutiny of circumstances in which Nagaon's Mumtaz Begum was sent to Bangladesh. Court warns Assam govt that it would presume a Foreigners' Tribunal's May 30 opinion declaring her a foreigner would be considered "not ready" if the state fails to establish when it was finalised.

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Sunday condemned the repeated attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz after two merchant ships carrying Indian seafarers came under attack.In a statement, the ministry said the recurring attacks on commercial shipping in the region were deeply concerning and risked further aggravating an already volatile situation."We condemn the attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz region on 11 October 2026. MT PETRO DOLPHIN was reportedly struck by a drone, with two of the 11 Indian seafarers onboard reported missing," it said."MT VALTHERA, a Marshall Islands-flagged tanker, was struck by an unknown projectile, resulting in a fire onboard. All 11 Indian seafarers onboard MT VALTHERA are reported to be safe. The Embassy of India in Muscat is closely monitoring the situation and coordinating with the Omani authorities and respective ship management companies for the rescue of missing Indians and to provide all possible assistance to the Indian crew," it added.MEA also reiterated the need for immediate de-escalation and a resolution to the ongoing conflict between the United States and Iran through dialogue and diplomacy."The safety and security of Indian seafarers remain a priority for the government of India. The recurring attacks on commercial shipping in the region are deeply concerning and risk further aggravating an already volatile situation," it said."India reiterates the need for immediate de-escalation and a resolution to the ongoing conflict through dialogue and diplomacy. Attacks on commercial vessels, seafarers and civilian infrastructure must cease. Freedom of navigation and the safe, unimpeded flow of maritime commerce through international waterways, in accordance with international law, must be upheld," it added.This comes after a vessel carrying 11 Indian seafarers came under a drone attack off the coast of Oman, leaving two crew members missing while nine were rescued.Indians have been facing dangers in the Middle East recently amid renewed tensions. On Saturday, 11 Indians were injured when Riyadh airport came under attack. A day later, the Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia announced that one of them had died.The embassy of India in Riyadh said it had been following up on Saturday's attack and was in touch with local authorities and hospital officials to enquire about the condition of the injured Indians.
Article Summary: MEA condemns repeated attacks on commercial vessels in Strait of Hormuz. Comes after vessel carrying 11 Indian seafarers came under a drone attack off Oman. Two crew members missing while nine were rescued. On Saturday, 11 Indians were injured when Riyadh airport came under attack.

NEW DELHI: CPM Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas on Sunday wrote to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and President Droupadi Murmu, Rajya Sabha Chairman CP Radhakrishnan alleging that he was assaulted by Delhi Police personnel while speaking to the media during protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He sought urgent intervention, an independent investigation and accountability, alleging a breach of parliamentary privilege.Brittas said the incident took place while he was exercising his democratic duty and interacting with the press."While peacefully interacting with journalists in connection with the ongoing democratic protests demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner, Shri Gyanesh Kumar, I was forcibly dragged away, bodily lifted by police personnel, assaulted inside a police vehicle and subsequently abandoned on the roadside. The incident raises grave questions concerning personal liberty, the right to peaceful expression, police accountability and compliance with the constitutional safeguards that this Hon'ble Court has time and again upheld and reaffirmed through its authoritative judgments," he said in his letter."The Government cannot intimidate democracy into silence. It cannot deploy the police as an instrument of political retaliation.It cannot substitute the force of the baton for the force of argument. And it cannot expect the people to surrender their constitutional freedoms merely because those in power find dissent inconvenient. Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(b) of the Constitution protect freedom of speech and peaceful assembly, while Article 21 safeguards life and personal liberty. Any restraint or detention must have a lawful basis, and any use of force must be necessary, lawful and proportionate. The brutal assault, the circumstances in which I was taken away, and the manner in which I was released demand urgent scrutiny under these constitutional guarantees and the applicable laws and Rules governing police conduct and detention," he added.Brittas also wrote separate letters to President Murmu and vice president, Rajya Sabha chair CP Radhakrishnan, while refering to Supreme Court directions. "The police atrocities raises serious questions under Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(b) of the Constitution, which protect freedom of speech and peaceful assembly, and Article 21, which safeguards life and personal liberty," he wrote in letter to the president.Meanwhile, addressing the Rajya Sabha chair, he cited "authoritative publication Rajya Sabha at Work" and said, "The matter, however, extends beyond the personal indignity and physical harm inflicted upon me. It raises a question of privilege and of the dignity and authority of the Rajya Sabha itself. I do not contend that membership of Parliament confers immunity from law. My submission is that the forcible manhandling and assault of a sitting Member, in circumstances where I was peacefully discharging my role as a public representative and had repeatedly identified myself, must be considered in the light of established parliamentary precedents concerning the treatment of Members by law-enforcement authorities,"The allegations came amid a fresh round of protests in the national capital on Sunday, when more than 200 demonstrators were detained as they attempted to march towards Jantar Mantar. The INDIA bloc is set to hold a march on Monday, with opposition leaders stepping up their criticism of the police action.The protests followed a security clampdown on Saturday, when thousands of demonstrators and several opposition leaders were detained as police prevented them from reaching Jantar Mantar. More than 30,000 police and paramilitary personnel were deployed across the capital as part of the security arrangements.The demonstrations have been called by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) and backed by opposition parties seeking Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. The allegations have been denied by officials.

NEW DELHI: Congress general secretary in-charge of Punjab Sachin Pilot on Sunday expressed confidence that his party would return to power in the state with an absolute majority, claiming that people had lost faith in the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government and wanted a change.Speaking to reporters at the Punjab Congress headquarters in Chandigarh, Pilot said voters wanted to bring the Congress back to power in the Assembly elections scheduled for early next year.“The Congress will form its government with absolute majority in Punjab,” Pilot said, alongside newly appointed Punjab Congress president Pargat Singh, according to news agency PTI.Singh, a three-time MLA from Jalandhar Cantt and former captain of the Indian hockey team, formally took charge as the Punjab Pradesh Congress Committee (PPCC) president at a ceremony at Punjab Congress Bhawan on Sunday.He replaced Ludhiana MP Amrinder Singh Raja Warring, who stepped down from the post earlier this month.Pilot acknowledged Warring's work during his four-and-a-half-year tenure as state Congress president and said Singh had now been entrusted with the responsibility of leading the party's state unit.“Pargat Singh has assumed his charge. Former Punjab Congress president Amrinder Singh Raja Warring worked very hard for four-and-a-half years.Now, Pargat Singh has been entrusted with the responsibility,” Pilot said.Pilot said Congress leaders were working together ahead of the Assembly elections, adding that four months remained for the polls.“People of Punjab have lost faith in AAP government and want 'badlav'. They want to get rid of this government,” he said, expressing confidence that voters would bring the Congress back to power.Singh, meanwhile, called for collective efforts to address the state's challenges.“We all will have to work hard together. Names of 13 crore voters have been cut. When irregularities will be committed in polls, so there will be reaction from public,” he said.He added that Congress leaders Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge stood with the people and democracy.Warring, who resigned as Punjab Congress president on October 1, said he would support Singh and continue working for the party, PTI reported.“There is no other objective. NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke shot back at the Delhi Police after they released a video claiming that while under detention, he was offered to speak to his family after his grandmother's demise.Dipke disputed the force's claim that he had declined assistance to contact his relatives and travel home for her last rites, saying he wasn't given his phone to access contacts.In a statement reacting to the police's account, Dipke said he had repeatedly requested access to his phone to retrieve his cousin's number and speak to a lawyer, but was denied both requests. He also questioned why officers asked him to call his father at 3.30 am and tell him that he could be sent to jail for a long time."I had requested to let me speak to my cousin who lives with my grandmother. The same father who has just lost his mother. How much more trauma did you want to put my family through after we already lost my grandmother?"Questioning the timing and purpose of the call, he added, "What was the purpose of trying to call my parents at f-ing 3:30 in the morning? You wanted to torment them?"Dipke's allegations came after Delhi Police released a video showing officers informing him of his grandmother's death while he was in detention in the national capital.Deputy Commissioner of Police Neha Yadav said officers approached the CJP founder after learning about the death and offered to help him contact his family, arrange flights and travel to his hometown for the funeral. They sensitively asked if he needed help with flights, phone calls, or anything else. They repeatedly asked if he wished to speak to his parents, but he declined,” DCP Yadav said.The police released the video after Dipke's mother, Anita Dipke, accused the force of lying about informing her son of the death. She had said the family was unable to contact him and had postponed the last rites until he could return home.Delhi Police maintained that Dipke had been informed about his grandmother's death and the scheduled funeral. It also said the offer to facilitate his travel was made on humanitarian grounds but was turned down.Dipke's paternal grandmother, Savitribai Shankarrao Dipke, 85, died at her home in Santuk Pimpri village in Maharashtra's Hingoli district at 11.30 am on Saturday. She had been unwell for a prolonged period and was suffering from age-related ailments.

NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) MP Bansuri Swaraj on Sunday accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal of engaging in a “competition of anarchy”, alleging that voters had rejected both parties and that their leaders were making excuses for their electoral defeats.Addressing a press conference at the BJP headquarters, the New Delhi MP said the Congress and AAP had failed to win the people's trust and were looking for reasons to explain their setbacks instead of engaging in constructive politics.“It appears a competition of anarchy is emerging between Arvind Kejriwal and Rahul Gandhi—whether it is the Aam Aadmi Party or the Congress party , the voters of this nation have rejected both. He also targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi by referring to the fictional villain Mogambo from the film Mr India.The Congress leader accused Union home minister Amit Shah's Delhi Police of resorting to “thuggery” and alleged that workers of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and BJP had been allowed to attack women and young protesters.“Amit Shah's Delhi Police has not only resorted to thuggery itself but is also giving a free hand and encouragement to the real goons of the RSS-BJP to perpetrate violence against women and the youth,” he said.He added that attempts to suppress young people would only intensify their anger.“As I had said, the more 'Mogambo Modi' and his government try to suppress them, the more the anger of Gen Z and the students will intensify,” Rahul said.Announcing the next protest, he said, “On Monday, October 12, the Congress, the entire INDIA alliance, and the youth of the country will once again take to the streets in large numbers. Article Summary: BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj accuses Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal of engaging in a “competition of anarchy” The remarks came amid a political confrontation over the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protests demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Article Title: A Texas family spent nearly eight years fighting over the 65,000-acre Brite Ranch, worth at least $60 million; days before trial, the heirs agreed to divide the historic property into four pieces
Article Text:
Four heirs, four portions of the ranch

How the family dispute began

A ranch with more than a century of history

A bitter family dispute over one of West Texas’s most historic ranches has taken an unexpected turn, with the heirs agreeing to divide the sprawling property rather than force a sale of the entire estate. The agreement involving the 65,000-acre Brite Ranch was reported by The Big Bend Sentinel on October 8, 2026, shortly before a jury trial was scheduled to begin. Court records from the Texas Court of Appeals and historical accounts published by the Texas State Historical Association provide further context on the dispute and the ranch’s legacy. The settlement brings the family closer to resolving a legal battle that began in 2018, when disagreements over trust management and the distribution of ranch income escalated into years of litigation. Valued at an estimated $60 million or more, the property has long been both a family asset and a significant part of Presidio County’s history.Under the proposed settlement, the ranch would be divided into four portions for Jim White, his brother Mac White, their sister Hester Ann White and Geoffrey Connor, the adopted son of Mac and the late Beau White. The agreement marks a major shift in the dispute. Hester Ann had opposed dividing the property and sought a court-ordered sale of the ranch as a single estate.However, a filing dated October 1 requested cancellation of the jury trial scheduled for October 21 and acknowledged her agreement to the division, according to The Big Bend Sentinel.The settlement does not necessarily mean every issue has been resolved. The newspaper reported that Jim, Cuatro White, Mac and Connor had also asked the district judge to retain the proceeding as a bench trial, potentially allowing the court to consider whether the allocation of land should be adjusted. They argued that Hester Ann had not contributed to certain ranch expenses and court-related costs. At the time of the newspaper’s report, the judge had not ruled on the request.The conflict dates to a lawsuit filed in 2018 by Mac and Beau against their brother Jim, who managed the ranch and served as trustee of the family trust that held its principal assets. The brothers alleged that Jim had breached his fiduciary duties, including by failing to distribute income fairly and by making decisions involving compensation for himself and family members working on the property. A jury trial in 2023 resulted in a judgment that removed Jim as trustee, awarded damages and divided the family trust into separate trusts. Former Texas Comptroller Susan Combs was appointed interim trustee to oversee financial administration.Jim and his supporters challenged the decision. In December 2024, the Eighth Court of Appeals in El Paso reversed the judgment and ordered a new trial, finding a fundamental error in the jury instructions. The ruling revived Jim’s position in the wider dispute and prolonged uncertainty over the ranch’s future.The litigation also became entangled in a dispute over Connor’s adoption by Mac and Beau in 2022. Some relatives challenged the adoption, alleging it was intended to affect inheritance interests. The allegations were contested, and the question of whether the adoption was improper was not resolved in the proceedings described by The Big Bend Sentinel. Years of court proceedings, disagreements over control of the land and the costs of litigation have now given way to an agreement that could finally establish separate ownership for the heirs.The Brite Ranch was established by Lucas Charles Brite, who began accumulating land in the region in the late 19th century. The operation became known for its Hereford cattle and grew into a major ranching enterprise in the Big Bend region of Texas. At its height, the original holdings extended across substantially more land than the current 65,000-acre property.Its history also includes a violent episode that became part of the region’s broader borderlands story. On Christmas Day in 1917, armed raiders attacked the ranch, looted its store and killed civilians. The raid was followed weeks later by the Porvenir Massacre, in which Texas Rangers and other armed men killed 15 Mexican and Mexican American men and boys. Historical accounts identify the killings as retaliation linked to suspicions surrounding the earlier raid, although the victims were not established to have participated in it.For many generations, the Brite family has played a significant role in the civic and political arenas of Presidio County. As a result, the ranch has come to symbolize much more than just a valuable tract of land; it is deeply intertwined with the area's cattle industry, local government dynamics, and the complex history associated with the border. The proposed division of the estate aims to allocate distinct portions to the heirs, transforming an estate that has remained central to their family legacy for decades. While it remains uncertain whether this settlement will put an end to the ongoing litigation, the court's management of the remaining issues will be pivotal. However, this agreement marks a noticeable shift away from the previously considered option of selling the historic ranch as an intact single property.What are your views on this? Tell us in the comments section below.
Article Summary: The Brite Ranch was established by Lucas Charles Brite in the late 19th century. The operation became known for its Hereford cattle and grew into a major ranching enterprise in the Big Bend region of Texas. On Christmas Day in 1917, armed raiders attacked the ranch, looted its store and killed civilians. The raid was followed weeks later by the Porvenir Massacre, in which Texas Rangers and other armed men killed 15 Mexican and Mexican American men and boys.

Article Title: Flash flood sweeps away 40 houses, 6 bridges in Nepal; up to 10 missing
Article Text:
100+ foreigners stuck in trekking region

A pre-dawn flash flood in Nepal’s Manaslu trekking region on Sunday swept away nearly 40 houses, six bridges and hydropower infrastructure. Up to 10 people are missing and more than 150 foreign tourists are stranded.Early SMS warnings helped residents flee to higher ground, while the Army rescued 49 people. Authorities ordered evacuations and alerted downstream districts.The disaster struck barely 45 days after catastrophic floods along Bhote Koshi-Trishuli river killed more than 1,450 people and left 5,250 missing. The latest flood struck around 4am along Budhi Gandaki, a tributary of Trishuli, in Chumnubri, approximately 100km west of Kathmandu.Authorities suspected a landslide had temporarily blocked a tributary, allowing water and debris to build up before the obstruction gave way. However, officials had yet to establish the exact cause. Five people, including two women and three men staying near Ungilung river, remained missing. Separately, four to five herders were also out of contact.The flood destroyed 35-40 houses and a primary school, leaving another 20-22 houses at risk.Six bridges were swept away or damaged, cutting off remote settlements.Floodwaters also destroyed the construction camp and equipment of the under-construction 341MW Budhi Gandaki hydropower project at Salleri. At Arughat, Budhi Gandaki river rose to 8.4m ag­ainst a danger level of 5m before floodwaters swept away the monitoring station, disrupting water-level readings.Authorities issued evacuation alerts across Dhading, Tanahun, Chitwan and East and West Nawalparasi, warning residents along Trishuli and Narayani rivers to stay away from riverbanks.National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority chief executive Dharmaraj Uprety said authorities could not rule out another blockage upstream. “However, we cannot yet say whether the river has been blocked again upstream or whether the danger has passed,” he said.Uprety said authorities received information about the flood at 6.20am and issued the first SMS warnings at 6.40am. Nearly 2 lakh alerts were sent in two rounds, urging resid­e­nts to move away from riverba­nks and vulnerable settleme­nts.The flood also disrupted the popular Manaslu trekking circuit during Nepal’s peak autumn tourist season, damagi­ng trails and suspension bridges. More than 100 foreign tourists were stranded at Jagat, a key entry point to the trekking region, while 17 were stuck at Lokpa and another 40 at Chhekampar in Chum Valley. Manaslu Conservation Area Project conservation officer Bhuvanraj Ojha told TOI the tourists were safe and authorities were arranging helicopter evacuations.
Article Summary: Flash flood in Nepal’s Manaslu trekking region on Sunday swept away nearly 40 houses, six bridges and hydropower infrastructure. Up to 10 people are missing and more than 150 foreign tourists are stranded. The Army rescued 49 people. Authorities ordered evacuations and alerted downstream districts.

Article Title: Watch: New footage shows moment missile hit Riyadh airport; 13 killed, including Indian national
Article Text:
CCTV footage captured from when a deadly strike hit a Saudi airport

Poll Vote & Share your view What measures should be taken to ensure the safety of travelers in conflict-affected areas? Increased military presence Improved intelligence and monitoring Better communication with travelers 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

New footage has been released by news outlet Al Arabiya showing the moment a strike hit King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, as passengers, including Umrah pilgrims preparing to board their flights, waited inside the terminal.The footage captures the moments surrounding the impact, bringing into focus the danger faced by civilians caught in the attack.The missile strike on Saturday, October 10, killed 13 people and injured more than 300 others, according to Saudi authorities. An Indian national was among those killed, while 11 Indians were injured, the Indian embassy in Riyadh said. The embassy said it was in touch with local authorities and hospital officials to monitor the condition of the injured and provide assistance.The Indian national who died was identified as Mohammed Yusuf, a 46-year-old IT professional from Hyderabad. According to sources, Yusuf, who was from Mehdipatnam, was waiting near a check-in kiosk with his family to travel to Medina for Umrah when the strike hit the airport. Debris from the impact reportedly fell on him, leaving him critically injured. He later died in hospital. His wife and two children, who were accompanying him, were also injured and were reported to be in critical condition.In a statement issued after his death, the Indian embassy said it would support the family and facilitate the early repatriation of his mortal remains. External affairs minister S Jaishankar also condoled the death, saying the embassy would extend all possible assistance to the bereaved family.The Saudi civil aviation authority identified the other victims as four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals and one person each from Palestine, the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria and Sudan.The attack was followed by another incident on Sunday, when an unidentified projectile struck a passenger terminal at Riyadh airport, according to the Saudi-led coalition fighting Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen. The projectile hit the complex housing terminals 3 and 4, which are used for domestic flights. Authorities did not immediately provide further details about Sunday's incident. The airport remained closed, while schools in Riyadh shifted to online classes.The latest incidents came amid repeated attacks targeting Saudi airports and oil installations. Yemen's Houthi movement, also known as Ansar Allah, has claimed responsibility for attacks on Saudi targets in recent days, but had not claimed responsibility for Saturday's deadly airport strike at the time of the reports.On Sunday, Houthi military spokesperson Brigadier General Yahya Saree warned airlines and travellers against using Saudi airports and airspace, saying they were vulnerable to attacks. Airports in Mecca and Medina were exempted from the warning.India's ministry of external affairs strongly condemned the repeated attacks on Riyadh's main airport, including the October 10 strike, describing attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure as “completely unacceptable” and calling for them to stop immediately. New Delhi also expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia and called for peace and normalcy to return to the region.
Article Summary: CCTV footage shows the moment a missile strike hit King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, on October 10. The strike killed 13 people and injured more than 300 others, including 11 Indians. The Indian national who died was identified as Mohammed Yusuf, a 46-year-old IT professional from Hyderabad.

Article Title: When Delhi cops played catch-up with protesters
Article Text:
AISA leader Neha Bora and several participants faced detention as police intervened, triggering a chaotic chase

Protecting the right to peaceful protest Maintaining law and order Balancing both rights and public safety 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





NEW DELHI: A chase through central Delhi ended in the detention of All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora, along with others, Sunday afternoon, as protesters renewed their attempt to march towards Jantar Mantar to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Bora was detained around 3pm after running towards Connaught Place with police personnel pursuing her and other demonstrators. The sequence began around 2.30pm, when protesters started gathering near RK Ashram Marg Metro station following her call to continue the agitation.A large contingent of police personnel moved towards the gathering, attempting to stop the march and taking several participants into custody.As police closed in, Bora was seen running towards CP, with several protesters following her past barricades as they then attempted to proceed towards Jantar Mantar. At 2.51 pm, Bora posted: "We have crossed the barricades and reached CP."Police personnel pursued the demonstrators through the streets before intercepting and detaining them. Cops were seen holding them by their arms and legs while dragging and carrying them towards waiting buses even as they kept struggling and resisting.In a video posted on X after her detention, Bora alleged that agitators were being held in cramped compartments inside a police bus. "These are the buses they are taking us in. This bus has four cells," she said. "There is no space to breathe."She claimed the windows had glass behind metal grilles and that several women were confined together in a small compartment. She also alleged that male protesters had been verbally abused and kicked in their private parts. Questioning the conditions in which they were being transported, she likened the compartments to jail cells and accused police of using excessive force.The attempted march followed a series of appeals by Bora to sustain the protests despite police curbs. Earlier Sunday, she had written on social media: "When those sworn to protect the Constitution look away, people must remind them what it demands. We cannot let this become normal. The fight for democracy continues, and we will not look away."Her call for Sunday's gathering followed a late-night post urging supporters to continue demonstrating despite Saturday's detentions."Let a hundred Jantar Mantars bloom! Another part of Delhi will become Jantar Mantar tomorrow," she wrote. Also Saturday, Bora had urged those unable to reach Jantar Mantar to regroup near Dilli Haat. They assembled in INA area, where police detained her and others.
Article Summary: All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora, along with others, were detained Sunday afternoon. The sequence began around 2.30pm, when protesters started gathering near RK Ashram Marg Metro station. Bora was detained around 3pm after running towards Connaught Place with police personnel pursuing her and other demonstrators.

Article Title: CJP protest fallout: Delhi eases curbs, 20+ FIRs filed as Abhijeet Dipke-police row escalates
Article Text:
Security personnel detain activists near Connaught Place Sunday





NEW DELHI: A day after Delhi turned into a fortress to stop the protest against the SIR at Jantar Mantar, some restrictions were eased for commuters Sunday. Entry/exit at metro stations was reopened and interned in central Delhi restarted.However, multiple FIRs, detentions and fresh demonstrations continued.Police and Abhijeet Dipke also traded charges regarding when the CJP founder was informed about his grandmother’s death and the police’s conduct during his detention.Police sources said more than 20 FIRs were registered in connection with Saturday’s protest for alleged violations of Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), for obstructing public servants in the discharge of their duties, assaulting police personnel and other offences.While police sources put the number of protesters detained at 400, other accounts claimed that over 700 people had been detained.Protests and marches continued at several locations, including Connaught Place and RK Ashram Marg, with demonstrators demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Police personnel remained deployed across sensitive areas to prevent gatherings and maintain law and order.In a relief to CJP’s three leading faces, an executive magistrate court ordered the release of Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who were placed under preventive arrest after arriving in the capital Saturday. They were released after an undertaking that they would not cause any “breach of peace” for a year.Dipke later rejected claims that he had signed any agreement. He said the outfit would continue its demonstrations against the CEC.Dipke spoke to the media in Nagpur Sunday evening after arriving on a flight from New Delhi, before leaving by road in a car for his hometown in Hingoli district following the death of his grandmother.In Delhi, Dipke visited advocate Kapil Sibal ’s house after being released by police. He alleged that after being detained at IGI Airport , he was not allowed to use his phone, contact his lawyer or speak to his cousin after learning about his grandmother’s death.“Delhi police woke me up at 3.30am today and asked me to call my parents and tell them that I had been arrested. My family is already mourning, and this would have been a bigger blow to them. It was very heartless behaviour,” he said. Delhi Police , meanwhile, released a video Sunday showing an officer informing Dipke about his grandmother’s death. A senior police officer said he had been informed around 2pm.In the video, the officer expressed condolences and offered to arrange for transport, including a bus or flight, if Dipke wished to attend the funeral. Dipke repeatedly responded, “I’ll stay,” when asked whether he wanted to leave.The officer also offered to facilitate a call with a family member through an official police number. When asked about speaking to his father, Dipke said he would not be able to speak to him.At one point, Dipke said, “Funeral kara do. Aaj hi kar do (Just arrange the funeral. Do it today).” The officer replied that the funeral had been scheduled for the following day and assured him that the police would try to facilitate any arrangements he needed.Dipke remained firm in his decision on not leaving. The officer told him he could inform the police if he changed his mind.In response to the video shared by the cops, Dipke posted on X: “Why did you delete the part where I was asking for my phone so I could retrieve my cousin’s number? And where I was asking to let me speak to my lawyers? The same Delhi Police, which is now taking the moral high ground for informing me about my grandmother’s demise and offering me a ride home, came to me at 3.30 in the morning with arrest papers, demanding that I sign them. Where did all that humanity go at 3.30am? Despite knowing that I had just lost my grandmother, they still insisted that I sign the arrest papers. I refused until I was allowed to speak to my lawyers.”
Article Summary: Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were released after an undertaking that they would not cause any “breach of peace” for a year. Police sources put the number of protesters detained at 400, other accounts claimed that over 700 people had been detained.

Article Title: After workload complaint, Mumbai’s Sion Hospital resident doctor dies by suicide
Article Text:
Dr Shivsharan Patil, a first-year junior resident, was a native of Karnataka.





MUMBAI: A first-year resident doctor at civic-run Sion Hospital was found dead by suicide in his hostel bathroom around 7.30pm on Saturday. Hospital officials said he was a surgery resident and had earlier complained of a heavy workload.Dr Shivsharan Patil, a first-year junior resident, was a native of Karnataka On Saturday, when his whereabouts were unknown for several hours, his roommate was asked to look for him. “When he called his phone, he heard it ringing inside the bathroom and alerted the senior authorities,” said a senior doctor from the hospital.Security guards were then called in and the door was broken open. Hospital authorities said that while there were complaints regarding workload in the past, none had reached them over the last couple of months, as the workload in the deceased doctor’s unit had lessened.Dr Patil was found with an injectable medical device. The hospital has not yet been informed of a suicide note by the Sion police. However, police have registered an accidental death report.Meanwhile, the hospital has contacted his family, and his body will be handed over to them after a post-mortem. While National Medical Commission’s (NMC) rules state that no resident may work beyond 48 hours a week, this is seldom followed within hospital settings.Past data from the Nagpur govt Medical College showed that one trainee logged more than 540 hours in a single month. At least 25 resident doctors have died by suicide over the last few years.Maharashtra Association of Resident Doctors (MARD) representative Dr Rutuja Raut said the association is collecting larger data on suicide by resident doctors due to heavy work pressure and will submit it to NMC.Need help?
