Article Summary: Dr Shivsharan Patil, a first-year junior resident, was a native of Karnataka. Hospital officials said he was a surgery resident and had earlier complained of a heavy workload. The hospital has not yet been informed of a suicide note by the Sion police.

Article Title: CJP raises ‘phone hacking’ doubts, to continue protest till CEC resigns
Article Text:
Ranka who, along with Das, is one of the co-conveners of CJP, called the CJP trio’s police detention a “kidnap”.





NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janata Party’s Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das at a news conference Sunday raised several questions and doubts regarding the action taken against them as well as thousands of protesters who came out to march on the outfit’s call.In a long interaction with journalists at the Press Club of India, along with CJP member Ratna Singh, SFI member Aishe Ghosh and other Left-backed student activists, Das spoke about the fear that their phones may have been hacked into after being seized.“We told the police they could take our phones, but they must provide a seizure memo and follow the law,” he said. "We were not even allowed to speak to our lawyers. Our phones were kept (from us) for more than 24 hours. We fear they may have been hacked or cloned (our phones), and that documents or evidence may have been planted against us, as has happened with other activists,” he said.The duo said the movement would continue till chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns. “Our protests will continue until accountability is fixed, not just in Delhi but across India,” Das said. CJP also alleged that “right-wing extremist groups” were attempting to provoke violence and had “misbehaved with women in Connaught Place.”Ranka said CJP members had attempted another march towards Jantar Mantar Sunday but were detained and assaulted. Members of Students’ Federation of India (SFI) and All India Students’ Federation (AISF) faced similar treatment at the hands of the cops, Ranka added.Das asked why the authorities were going to such lengths to protect Kumar. “What information does Kumar have about govt or its leadership?” he asked.Ranka who, along with Das, is one of the co-conveners of CJP, called the CJP trio’s police detention a “kidnap”. The three were plucked out of a flight Saturday morning when they landed in Delhi. They were released Sunday morning.CJP also alleged that student leaders and protesters were being detained and beaten up. “If they think this will break our spirit, they are mistaken,” they said.The outfit alleged that Dipke, whose grandmother died Saturday during his detention, was denied contact with his family.Das also brought an allegation of custodial torture of protesters and questioned the lack of intervention by National Human Rights Commission. Criticising the restrictions on reporters that police had laid down, he said: “This is an Emergency-like situation for journalism.” He said the more than 40,000 security personnel at Jantar Mantar had made the place a fortress, inconveniencing residents.He also wondered why govt had not called them for a dialogue.CJP legal affairs head Ratna Singh alleged: “I was followed, my car was chased, and I was photographed as though I were a criminal.” .Singh said that 30 to 35 police personnel surrounded her and told her that she could do one of two things -- either accompany them to a detention centre or return home and remain there. She said she was held inside a car. “How can a citizen be kept in wrongful confinement like this?” she asked.Viraaj Devang, the national president of AISF, who was also at the news conference, said: “Delhi was turned into a cantonment. Ordinary citizens were effectively placed under house arrest, while many protesters arriving from outside Delhi were detained.”SFI national joint secretary Ghosh also questioned the manner in which protesters and activists were detained. Referring to the detention of Dhruv Rathee, she said: “People who were not in uniform entered Dhruv Rathee’s home and took him away without a warrant. This cannot be called the rule of law.”In a message directed at Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Rathee Sunday warned against suppressing dissent to the point where people no longer fear the consequences of speaking out.Dipke, who was not at the news conference as he had returned to Maharashtra to be with his family, posted on X: “Modi, as PM, is an embarrassment to India. Never has this country seen a bigger coward and bully.”He was also asked online if he had signed a bond to discontinue protesting. He wrote, “Haven’t signed any bond that says we won’t protest. We will hit the streets again”.Ranka said Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah were to blame for the breach of peace. The restrictions and detentions had damaged India’s image in the world, he said.Shortly after the news conference ended, commotion broke out at Press Club of India as police entered the premises. CJP members attempted to leave through the rear gate. Police, after failing to find them at the news conference venue, rushed towards the rear exit. The resulting commotion took some time to subside.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janata Party’s Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das at a news conference Sunday raised several questions and doubts regarding the action taken against them. Thousands of protesters who came out to march on the outfit's call. CJP also alleged that “right-wing extremist groups” were attempting to provoke violence.

Article Title: 'Dad will take care of it': 3 killed as speeding Mini Cooper driven by ‘drunk’ 19-year-old rams scooter near Kochi airport
Article Text:
A speeding luxury hatchback driven by Suhail Sajeev crashed into a scooter, killing three youths instantly.





KOCHI: Three youths were killed when a speeding Mini Cooper, driven by Alappuzha South native Sajeev Jamal's son Suhail (19) rammed their scooter at 1.45am on Sunday on the airport road along Nedumbassery.Police arrested an 'inebriated' Suhail on charges of culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The deceased were identified as Devika (21) of Wayanad, Gopika (22) of Palakkad and Iyas (21) of Coorg, Karnataka.CCTV footage showed the premium hatchback hitting the two-wheeler from behind and the passengers being thrown off on impact. The victims were killed on the spot and the scooter landed some distance away. People rushed them to Desom CA hospital and Angamaly Taluk Hospital where the youths were declared dead.Nedumbassery Police said that the trio were employees of a craft shop in Thrikkakara and had gone to a tea shop near the airport. They were heading to Athani when the car rammed their scooter. The front portion of the car was mangled in the crash.District Police Chief (Ernakulam Rural) KS Sudarshan said police took Suhail into custody from the spot and the team completed his medical examination immediately. He said they took blood and urine samples for forensic examination.Sudarshan said although the reports of his blood sample are awaited, preliminary probe indicated that he was inebriated. When asked if he was driving under the influence of other intoxicants, he said the police took samples to check the same and further action would be taken based on medical reports.Soon after the accident, videos from an Instagram page, purportedly belonging to Suhail, were shared widely on social media. One of them was an Instagram story that showed the car rocketing at a speed of 220km/hr during a highway ride. Sudarshan said his team had taken note of the incident and the driver's background will be investigated."We have cameras on these routes. If such activities happened in the past, we will investigate them," he said. Reacting to reports that Suhail's co-passenger had quarrelled with first responders, he said that they will collect statements and act accordingly. He added that further sections can be added against Suhail as and when an offence is detected. A detailed forensic examination of the car was held.The SP said the team will look into public concerns that car races are happening in the region. "Witnesses said the car was speeding and we suspect it was over 120km/hr," said the officer.People confronted Suhail when police took him to a hospital for medical examination. Amid reports that his co-passenger, Ninav (19), told first responders that his father will take care of things, some individuals, who were at the hospital, asked him about his father's whereabouts. Police had to use force to protect him from the ire of the public.Meanwhile, excise department began an inquiry into bars that allegedly served alcohol to Suhail, who is below the legal drinking age of 23.Police have also arrested Ninav.
Article Summary: Police arrested an 'inebriated' Suhail on charges of culpable homicide not amounting to murder. CCTV footage showed the premium hatchback hitting the two- wheeler from behind. The victims were killed on the spot and the scooter landed some distance away.

Article Title: ‘Unofficial house arrest’: After release, YouTuber Dhruv Rathee claims cops still stationed outside Gurgaon home
Article Text:
YouTuber Dhruv Rathee was forcibly taken from his home and detained by police for over 20 hours





GURGAON: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, who was prevented by police from joining Saturday's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest, described his detention as an act of 'kidnapping'.Rathee, an Indian citizen who lives in Germany and came here for the protest, said in a video post he was released by cops around 3am on Sunday after being held in detention for over 20 hours without access to a lawyer or phone.He also alleged his parents were manhandled during the detention, accusing the Centre of creating an "unofficial Emergency".In the video, posted at 11.19am on Sunday, Rathee alleged that he was forcibly taken from his bedroom without even being allowed time to wear his slippers. He also claimed that he was assaulted and had sustained injuries all over his body."These people have literally sent 'gundas' to kidnap me. There were more than 50 'gundas' outside my house... I was dragged from my bedroom like a criminal," he said.According to sources, Rathee returned to his parents' house in Kendriya Vihar, Sector 56, on Sunday morning amid police presence, with around 50 personnel in plain clothes gathered near his apartment complex.The detention came amid protests in Delhi led by the CJP demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The demonstrations on Saturday were met with extensive security arrangements, barricading, traffic restrictions and detentions of protesters.Recounting the events of Saturday morning, Rathee alleged that around 20 men in plain clothes entered his house around 7am while he was still asleep. His mother, who opened the door after hearing a commotion outside, was allegedly pushed aside as the group entered the house and moved towards his bedroom."Before I could react, these people literally kidnapped me. The operation did not follow procedure expected during an arrest or detention. They literally dragged me out of the bedroom, took me down the stairs. I have injuries all over my body," he alleged.Rathee claimed that even his parents' phones were seized, leaving them unable to record the incident. The YouTuber was kept in detention at Sector 39 crime branch after he was picked up from his home."They kept me confined for 20 hours, neither allowed me to access a phone, nor allowed me to speak to a lawyer. The police personnel kept telling me that it was neither an arrest nor a detention and that I would be released." Rathee said in the video.Questioning the circumstances in which he was taken from his home, Rathee said he would have accompanied the police willingly had an officer identified himself, explained the legal provisions, and asked him to visit a police station.He claimed that around 15 police personnel had been stationed around his house after his release, monitoring his movements and effectively placing him under what he described as unofficial house arrest.He said he would not back down. "I will continue to raise my voice for the country in this same way no matter how much you try to suppress me," he said.
Article Summary: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee claims he was forcibly taken from his home and detained by police for over 20 hours. Rathee, an Indian citizen who lives in Germany and came here for the protest, said in a video post he was released by cops around 3am on Sunday. He also alleged his parents were manhandled during the detention, accusing the Centre of creating an "unofficial Emergency"

Article Title: ASI gunned down in Tarn Taran; 5th cop to be murdered in Punjab this year
Article Text:
Iqbal Singh, an assistant sub-inspector from Punjab, tragically lost his life to violent assailants

Targeted attacks





CHANDIGARH: An assistant sub-inspector (ASI) with the counter-intelligence wing was shot dead by two motorcycle-borne assailants while returning home after duty late Sunday evening. Iqbal Singh (55) is the fifth policeman to be murdered in Punjab this year.A resident of Naushera Pannuan, around 15 km from Tarn Taran, Iqbal sustained at least two bullet injuries in the attack, and died on the spot. The killers sped away and are yet to be identified.Tarn Taran SSP Surendra Lamba said, "The ASI was posted in Makhu (70 km from Amritsar). He was being followed by two bike-borne assailants who shot two to three bullets at him between 6:15 pm and 6:30 pm on Louhka Road in Tarn Taran district. We have got some leads and hope to trace the accused soon."As per initial information, the ASI was driving back after a "private visit" and wasn't in uniform, said the SSP.A senior police officer said Iqbal’s nephew is Ajmeet Singh, an accused in the 2022 Sarhali police station RPG attack case, who was shot dead in Naushera Pannuan on Sept 11 while on bail.According to sources, investigators are examining if the two murders are connected.The accused in Ajmeet’s killing was injured in a police encounter and arrested. “We are investigating the organised crime angle and revenge killings by gangsters,” said a senior police officer.Police are also examining a social media post in which gangsters Doni Bal, Prabh Dasuwal, Mohabbat Randhawa, Afridi Toot, Amar Khabbe and Shaganpreet purportedly took responsibility for Iqbal’s murder.The post claimed that the ASI was close to “our rival Landa Harike”, and hinted at a revenge killing over the murder of a sarpanch. The same group had claimed responsibility for Ajmeet’s murder.The slain ASI was earlier posted in Ferozepur counterintelligence and had been transferred to Tarn Taran recently. “There is a high probability this was a targeted killing by an organised crime network. We are investigating the case from all angles,” said the SSP.The murder is the latest in a series of attacks on police officials in Punjab. On Feb 22, ASI Gurnam Singh and home guard Ashok Kumar were shot dead inside a police station in Gurdaspur.On May 24, ASI Joga Singh was shot dead in Majitha and on Sept 17, ASI Harjit Singh was shot dead in Amritsar. On Sept 12, ASI Jaswant Singh narrowly survived a murder bid in Amritsar, and on Oct 4, ASI Sukhchain Singh was injured after being shot at in Ajnala.The attacks have triggered criticism from opposition parties. Former Punjab Congress chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring said, “Punjab is bleeding, and Bhagwant Mann’s govt has serious questions to answer... Repeated shootings and killings are creating fear across Punjab. Bhagwant Mann, how many more lives must be lost before your govt wakes up? When police personnel themselves are being targeted, what sense of security can ordinary citizens expect?”Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon posted on X: “In a Punjab where even those in uniform are not safe, who can the common Punjabi rely on? On one side, grand advertising claims about law and order; on the other, blood spilling on the streets. AAP has completely failed on the law and order front.”SAD functionary Bikram Singh Majithia alleged that CM Bhagwant Mann has “badly failed to maintain law and order in Punjab”. “CM is busy criticizing opponents and entertaining people with jokes while murderers continue to ambush and attack our police personnel… Arvind Kejriwal is taking Punjab back to the era it was engulfed in violence,” Majithia tweeted.
Article Summary: Iqbal Singh is the fifth policeman to be murdered in Punjab this year. The killers sped away and are yet to be identified. The ASI was driving back after a "private visit" and wasn't in uniform. Police are investigating the organised crime angle and revenge killings by gangsters.

Article Title: Muezzin arrested, cop suspended for ‘loud’ azaan in UP
Article Text:
A muezzin from a mosque found himself in legal trouble for reportedly breaching noise pollution regulations during the azaan





BIJNOR: A mosque muezzin was arrested and sent to jail after Bijnor DM and SP heard an allegedly loud azaan while travelling to a public grievance hearing in Najibabad on Saturday. Police seized the mosque’s loudspeaker and suspended a beat constable for negligence.The incident also prompted a district-wide order requiring police stations to submit affidavits confirming that loudspeakers at religious places complied with prescribed noise limits.DM Umesh Pratap Singh and SP Krishna Kumar Bishnoi were passing through Mohalla Maqbara on their way to a Samadhan Diwas hearing when they heard the azaan being played at an allegedly excessive volume.Bishnoi directed Kotwali police to take action, following which station in-charge Amit Kumar Malik reached the mosque, seized the loudspeaker and detained muezzin Mohammad Faizan.On a complaint by sub-inspector Saurabh Kumar, police registered an FIR against Faizan for allegedly violating noise pollution norms.They also initiated proceedings against him for breach of peace, following which a sub-divisional magistrate’s court sent him to jail.Police subsequently suspended beat constable Lalit Kumar for allegedly failing to enforce noise restrictions in the area.Following the incident, police directed all station in-charges across Bijnor to submit affidavits through their beat constables certifying that loudspeakers at religious places in their jurisdictions operated within permissible limits.They warned that future violations could invite action against the station in-charge and beat personnel concerned.The action followed a district-wide police drive against loudspeakers at religious places in Sept, during which authorities reportedly removed 2,509 loudspeakers, including 1,323 from mosques, 1,116 from temples and 70 from gurdwaras.Religious institutions were also instructed to ensure that remaining loudspeakers operated within prescribed noise limits.Additional SP Krishna Gopal Singh said police were conducting a district-wide campaign to enforce govt and court directions on noise pollution.“Loudspeakers operating beyond the prescribed noise limits will not be allowed at religious places. Caretakers of all religious institutions have been instructed to follow the rules. Police station in-charges have also been directed to ensure compliance in their respective areas,” he said.In an Oct 1 order concerning a mosque in Saharanpur, Allahabad high court directed authorities not to interfere with the five daily azaans as long as the mosque complied with noise pollution rules.The court reiterated that using loudspeakers was not an essential religious practice protected under Article 25 of the Constitution and that their operation remained subject to the Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000.
Article Summary: Bijnor DM and SP heard an allegedly loud azaan while travelling to a public grievance hearing in Najibabad on Saturday. Police seized the mosque’s loudspeaker and suspended a beat constable for negligence. The incident prompted a district-wide police drive against loudspeakers at religious places.

Article Title: ​CJP's Abhijeet Dipke misses grandma’s funeral; Delhi Police and family trade charges
Article Text:
The death has triggered a bitter clash of narratives between Dipke’s family and Delhi Police





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke’s family cremated his paternal grandmother, nearly 24 hours after her death, in Hingoli district on Sunday, before he could return home following his detention, and release, by Delhi Police The death has triggered a bitter clash of narratives between Dipke’s family and Delhi Police over whether authorities informed him in time and facilitated his journey home.On Sunday morning, Abhijeet Dipke’s mother, Anita, accused Delhi Police of preventing the family from contacting her son and denied police claims that he had been adequately informed about his grandmother’s death.Delhi Police rejected the allegation. “The information regarding the demise of Dipke’s grandmother was promptly conveyed to him with due sensitivity. He was also informed of the scheduled funeral time and offered all possible assistance to facilitate his travel to his hometown on humanitarian grounds. However, he denied to avail the same,” Delhi Police said in a social media post.Police also released CCTV footage from the detention facility to support their version.Dipke, who reached Nagpur on Sunday afternoon while travelling to his native village in Hingoli district after his release, contested the police account.He alleged that officers refused to let him speak to his cousin, who lived with his grandmother, and denied him access to his phone.“I was asking for my phone so I could retrieve my cousin’s number. Delhi Police has deleted that portion of the CCTV footage,” he alleged. In a social media post, Dipke accused the police of showing little compassion during his detention.“The same Delhi Police which is now taking the moral high ground for informing me about my grandmother’s demise and offering me a ride home came to me at 3.30am with arrest papers and demanded that I sign them. Where did all that humanity go at 3.30am? Even after knowing I had lost my grandmother, they insisted that I sign the papers. I refused until I was allowed to speak to my lawyers,” he wrote.The dispute added a fresh political edge to an already tense standoff between Dipke and authorities. Emerging from detention, Dipke said the CJP would resume its protests and declared that he had not signed any undertaking promising to stay away from future agitations. “Put me in jail a hundred times. We are not afraid of your dictatorship. We will end this dictatorship,” he told reporters in Nagpur.Earlier, he had posted on social media that the party would neither “back down nor be intimidated”, describing Oct 10 as “the beginning of the end of this dictatorship.”
Article Summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke's family cremated his paternal grandmother, nearly 24 hours after her death, in Hingoli district on Sunday. The death has triggered a bitter clash of narratives between Dipke’s family and Delhi Police over whether authorities informed him in time.

Article Title: Oil prices today: Brent crude declines as Trump announces Russia-Ukraine energy truce
Article Text:
Russian diesel supplies ease market concerns.

Oil prices fell on Monday as expectations of additional Russian diesel supplies and a possible halt to attacks on energy facilities in the Russia-Ukraine conflict eased some concerns over supply. However, continued tensions in the Middle East kept Brent crude above $100 a barrel.Brent crude futures fell $1.54, or 1.47%, to $103.18 a barrel by 7.24 am IST. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude declined by the same amount, or 1.68%, to $90.31 a barrel.ICE gasoil futures, a benchmark for diesel, fell 3% to $1,436 per barrel after US President Donald Trump said Russia would supply additional diesel to US and global markets.Earlier on Friday, Trump said that Russia would immediately supply more than 300,000 metric tonnes of diesel, equivalent to around 2.25 million barrels.He added that another 500,000 tonnes would be supplied in November, followed by a further 1 million tonnes “immediately thereafter”.Global daily diesel consumption is forecast to be close to 29 million barrels, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA).Trump also announced on Sunday that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to halt attacks on each other’s energy facilities. However, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he was still waiting for details of the proposed energy ceasefire.The announcements eased some immediate concerns over supply, said Tim Waterer, chief analyst at KCM Trade, Reuters reported.“Questions remain over the validity and longevity of any such ceasefire, and without clearer evidence that it will actually hold, the extent of the pullback is likely to stay limited,” he added.Despite the easing of some supply concerns, the conflict in the Middle East continued to support oil prices. The Houthis claimed responsibility for a Saturday strike on Riyadh's international airport that reportedly killed 13 people and injured more than 300.Saudi authorities also reported injuries in another attack on the airport on Sunday.Trump said on Saturday that the US was considering joining Saudi strikes against the Houthis. The conflict has spilled over from the wider war involving Iran, launched by the US and Israel in February.Attacks on tankers passing through the Strait of Hormuz have also increased this month, threatening to disrupt the recovery in Middle Eastern crude exports seen in September.Goldman Sachs raised its Brent crude price forecast for December to $90 a barrel from $85, according to a note by analysts led by Daan Struyven.“We maintain our base case that continued adaptation of Mideast supply will eventually reduce crude oil prices, while potential renewed escalation still poses significant net upside risk,” the analysts said, estimating a risk premium of just over $20 a barrel.“We forecast WTI prices, which are unusually low vs Brent because of high US-Europe shipping costs, to average $81 in December 2026 and $73 in 2027,” they added.Oil prices ended the previous week with mixed movements. Brent futures for December delivery rose $2.47, or 2.41%, to $104.72 a barrel, while WTI gained 1% to settle at $91.85 a barrel.With Brent crude trading above $100 a barrel, geopolitical developments are likely to remain a key driver of prices. Progress in US-Iran negotiations could ease pressure, but the risk of renewed attacks, shipping disruptions and prolonged supply constraints is expected to keep volatility elevated.
Article Summary: ICE gasoil futures, a benchmark for diesel, fell 3% to $1,436 per barrel. US President Donald Trump said Russia would supply additional diesel to US and global markets. Trump also announced on Sunday that Ukraine and Russia had agreed to halt attacks on each other’s energy facilities.

Article Title: Manipur on boil again: Naga body gives 48-hour ultimatum to return man’s severed head
Article Text:
At least nine people were killed in separate firing incidents in Manipur on Friday and Saturday

Poll Vote & Share your view What is your opinion on the ultimatum issued by the Joint Tribes Council Manipur? It is justified It is excessive 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

(With agency inputs)





IMPHAL: A Naga civil society organisation has issued a 48-hour ultimatum demanding the return of the severed head of a man allegedly killed by armed groups in Manipur’s Kangpokpi district.According to news agency PTI, the headless body of 52-year-old Ajinbou R, who was allegedly killed in a suspected militant attack on Makui Ashang village in Kangpokpi district on Saturday, was brought to the Jawaharlal Nehru Institute of Medical Sciences in Imphal for a post-mortem on Sunday night.A video purportedly showing Ajinbou’s head among heavily armed militants dressed in camouflage went viral on Saturday.In a statement on Sunday, the Joint Tribes Council Manipur said, "The head of Ajinbou R remains missing. Post-mortem will not be conducted till his head is returned to his family members for a dignified burial. We will not allow state machinery to mutilate the remains further while his head is treated as a trophy by militants."Holding state and Central governments directly responsible for the renewed violence, it said, "This heinous crime is an affront to humanity."The council issued a "non-negotiable 48-hour ultimatum" to locate and return the severed head, failing which it warned of taking the "most stringent measures" to secure justice.At least nine people were killed in separate firing incidents in Manipur’s Kamjong, Ukhrul and Kangpokpi districts on Friday and Saturday, triggering a fresh wave of violence in the state.The violence began on Friday night when unidentified assailants shot dead a 22-year-old mother of five in Chassad village, a Kuki-dominated area in Naga-majority Kamjong district. Her killing triggered an exchange of fire between Kuki and Naga armed groups that continued until Saturday morning.Chief minister Y Khemchand Singh has condemned the killings and asked the authorities concerned to take immediate and "effective steps to control the situation, restore peace and order and ensure the safety and security of all citizens".More than 50 people have been killed and dozens of houses torched in violence between Kuki and Naga tribes since February this year.
Article Summary: The headless body of 52-year-old Ajinbou R was brought to the Jawaharlal Nehru Institute of Medical Sciences in Imphal for a post-mortem on Sunday night. At least nine people were killed in separate firing incidents in Manipur on Friday and Saturday.

Article Title: Hyderabad techie was waiting to check in for Madina flight when killed in Riyadh airport missile strike
Article Text:
Mohammed Yusuf, an IT professional from Hyderabad, was critically injured in a missile attack at an airport





HYDERABAD: A 46-year-old man from Hyderabad has reportedly died after being injured in the missile attack at King Khalid International Airport in Saudi capital Riyadh Saturday, which left 13 dead and over 300 injured.Some members of his family who were with him at the airport are also said to be in critical condition.According to sources, Mohammed Yusuf, an IT professional from Mehdipatnam, was waiting with his family near a check-in kiosk to travel to Madina for Umrah when a projectile struck the airport premises. Debris from the impact reportedly fell on Yusuf, leaving him critically injured.He later succumbed to his injuries at a hospital. The ministry of external affairs, in an X post Sunday, confirmed his death. "We are in touch with the family and will provide all support for ensuring the early repatriation of mortal remains," MEA said in the post.Hyderabad MP and AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi also posted on X about the incident and urged EAM S Jaishankar to provide "every possible assistance" to the family. "It's been confirmed that Yousuf sahab has passed away in the attack. His son is undergoing knee surgery, another son is in the hospital and 3 of his toes have been cut off.His daughter and wife are safe. His aunt (chachi) was with them and suffered injuries to the head but is out of danger. I am in touch with Yousuf's brother-in-law in Riyadh and the deputy chief of mission has assured me that they're taking care," he wrote.Saudi's General Authority of Civil Aviation announced Saturday (Oct 10) that operations at King Khalid International Airport had been temporarily suspended following the attack to allow authorities to assess the damage and verify the safety of airport facilities. According to reports, the fatalities included four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals, and one national each from the US, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan.
Article Summary: Mohammed Yusuf, an IT professional from Hyderabad, was waiting with his family near a check-in kiosk to travel to Madina for Umrah when a projectile struck the airport premises. Debris from the impact reportedly fell on Yusuf. He later succumbed to his injuries at a hospital.

Article Title: Tukaram Mundhe named secretary of panel probing MPSC paper leaks as chairman goes on leave
Article Text:
Tukaram Mundhe named MPSC paper leak panel secretary as chairman Vivek Bhimanwar goes on leave





MUMBAI: Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) chairman Vivek Bhimanwar announced early Monday that he was going on leave until the judicial inquiry into alleged paper leaks and the commission’s functioning is completed.The state government has set up a high-level, five-member inquiry committee headed by former Chief Justice of the Allahabad High Court Dilip Bhosale to probe allegations of paper leaks and recommend an overhaul of the MPSC’s functioning.IAS officer Tukaram Mundhe has been appointed secretary of the committee. Soon after Bhimanwar announced his decision to go on leave, MPSC aspirants ended their 10-day agitation in Pune early Monday.“MPSC students' satyagraha finally victorious. Victory of unity, determination.. and perseverance,” NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar, who was leading the protests, said in a post on X.“The state government has announced a judicial inquiry into the MPSC paper leak case. Throughout my entire life, I have always prioritized ethics. Therefore, I have decided to go on leave during this period instead of continuing to serve in the post until this inquiry is completed.The autonomy, credibility, and interests of students of the MPSC have always been my priority, and they will continue to be so in the future,” Bhimanwar said in a post on X.Hundreds of students had been protesting against alleged paper leaks in the MPSC and demanding reforms in Pune. The agitation was led and supported by NCP (SP) MLA Rohit Pawar and Congress MLA Vishwajeet Kadam.The protesters’ main demands included action and accountability over the Drug Inspector examination paper-leak controversy, the removal or resignation of MPSC chairman Vivek Bhimanwar, administrative reforms and a preference for offline examinations.Bhimanwar was appointed MPSC chairman in December 2025, sworn in in February 2026 and assumed charge in March. A 2009-batch IAS officer, he previously served as transport commissioner and private secretary to Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis.Earlier this month, the state government terminated the deputation of MPSC secretary Mahendra Harpalkar amid allegations of question paper leaks and irregularities in examinations conducted by the commission.Harpalkar had been appointed to the MPSC post on a two-year deputation in December 2025. An October 1 order issued by the state General Administration Department (GAD) said his appointment had been terminated for administrative reasons and that a separate order regarding his next posting would be issued.The order also directed Harpalkar to immediately hand over charge as MPSC secretary to another officer, with the commission’s consent.
Article Summary: Vivek Bhimanwar announced he was going on leave until the judicial inquiry into alleged paper leaks is completed. The state government has set up a high-level, five-member inquiry committee headed by former Chief Justice of the Allahabad High Court Dilip Bhosale. IAS officer Tukaram Mundhe has been appointed secretary of the committee.

Article Title: JNU row: FIR registered for sexual harassment against Congress MP Bimol Akoijam
Article Text:
Delhi Police has lodged an FIR against Angomcha Bimol Akoijam in response to allegations of sexual harassment from his students

Delhi Police registers FIR under BNS Sections 75 and 79

Why was JNU professor Angomcha Bimol Akoijam dismissed?

Congress MP calls JNU dismissal a ‘witch hunt’





NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has registered an FIR following a complaint by Jawaharlal Nehru University ’s (JNU) chief security officer, invoking provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) relating to sexual harassment and insulting the modesty of a woman.The FIR, registered at Vasant Kunj North police station on October 11, mentions the name of Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam in its details, and an investigation is underway.The FIR has been registered under Sections 75, 75(1)(i), 75(1)(iv) and 79 of the BNS. The development comes amid the controversy surrounding Akoijam, who was dismissed from his position as a JNU professor on Friday following an internal inquiry into sexual harassment allegations made by students.Section 75 of the BNS deals with sexual harassment, including unwelcome physical contact and advances, demands for sexual favours, showing pornography against a woman’s will and making sexually coloured remarks. Section 79 deals with words, gestures or acts intended to insult the modesty of a woman.The FIR was registered on the complaint of JNU’s chief security officer. Its details mention Akoijam, who represents the Inner Manipur constituency in the Lok Sabha.Police have not provided further details about the allegations recorded in the FIR in the information currently available.JNU dismissed Akoijam, who was associated with the Centre for the Study of Social Systems, with immediate effect on October 9 after an inquiry into sexual harassment allegations levelled against him by 11 students.The university’s Internal Committee recommended a major penalty under the Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965.The complaints reportedly included allegations of sexually suggestive remarks during vivas and classes, inappropriate advances at gatherings at the professor’s on-campus residence, and offers of higher marks in exchange for sexual favours.Akoijam has denied wrongdoing and criticised the university’s handling of the matter, describing his dismissal as a “witch hunt”.He said he had not received the Internal Committee’s recommendations or the formal dismissal order and demanded that the evidence against him be made public.He also said he intended to challenge the university’s decision through legal channels.The latest FIR is now under investigation by Delhi Police.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Delhi Police has lodged an FIR against Angomcha Bimol Akoijam in response to allegations of sexual harassment from his students. Delhi Police has registered an FIR following a complaint by Jawaharlal Nehru University ’s (JNU) chief security officer. The development comes amid the controversy surrounding A Koijam, who was dismissed from his position as a JNU professor on Friday.

Article Title: Former Rajasthan BJP MLA Atar Singh Bhadana beaten to death with sticks, stones amid stone crusher dispute
Article Text:
Bhadana died during treatment at the SMS Hospital

(With agency inputs)





JAIPUR: Former BJP MLA Atar Singh Bhadana was killed after he was allegedly attacked by a group of villagers over a dispute regarding the reopening of a stone crusher in Rajasthan’s Bharatpur district, police said on Monday.The incident took place on Sunday night in Bhonda village, where Bhadana had gone to his stone crusher site.Bhadana and local villagers had been involved in a dispute over the crusher for some time.According to news agency PTI, circle officer (Bhusawar) Neeraj Bhardwaj said Bhadana and his associate, Gagan Sharma, were allegedly attacked with sticks and stones during the confrontation.Both sustained serious injuries and were initially taken to a hospital in Weir. Bhadana was later referred to SMS Hospital in Jaipur, while Sharma was referred to a hospital in Bharatpur.Bhadana died during treatment at the SMS Hospital, he said.Police said villagers had accused Bhadana of encroaching on grazing land and carrying out illegal mining activities. The crusher had remained closed for about a year, and efforts to restart it had led to further disagreements.Villagers claimed they had been staging a peaceful protest for the past 10 to 15 days against the proposed reopening of the stone crusher.They alleged that Bhadana arrived at the site with around 40 to 50 people on Sunday evening and tried to remove them from the protest site, triggering a confrontation.Both sides have accused each other of assault.Additional police personnel have been deployed in the village to maintain law and order.Bhardwaj said the body had been kept in the mortuary for a post-mortem.
Article Summary: Bhadana and local villagers had been involved in a dispute over the crusher for some time. The crusher had remained closed for about a year, and efforts to restart it had led to further disagreements. Villagers claimed they had been staging a peaceful protest for the past 10 to 15 days.

Article Title: '24-hour ultimatum': CJP asks Delhi Police to fix date, time for Jantar Mantar protest
Article Text:
CJP activist Saurav Das said the party was willing to let the police decide the date and time for the protest.

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you support the Cockroach Janta Party approach to engaging with the police? Yes, it's proactive. No, it's confrontational. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

(With agency inputs)





NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) activists visited Parliament Street Police Station on Monday to seek a date for their proposed protest at Jantar Mantar, giving Delhi Police 24 hours to respond.CJP activist Saurav Das said the party was willing to let the police decide the date and time for the protest."Police tells everyone to approach them 10 days in advance. We are now saying that they have the choice to tell us the date and time (for protest at Jantar Mantar). We are giving them 24-hour ultimatum," Das told news agency ANI.CJP activist Ashutosh Ranka said the party would seek a date for the protest from Delhi Police and expressed hope that the authorities would respond."We are going to ask Delhi Police for a date to hold a protest at Jantar Mantar. We hope the police will give us a date. If they do not, we will make another call within 24 hours..." Ranka said."Peaceful protest is a right, a constitutional right, and people are already exercising it. People will protest peacefully. The police always complain that we should approach them 10 days in advance," Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) chief spokesperson Saurav Das told news agency PTI."We are now leaving the choice to them and asking them to specify the date and time. However, we will not let them keep the matter pending. We will give them a 24-hour ultimatum. Let's see," Das added.
Article Summary: CJP activist Saurav Das said the party was willing to let the police decide the date and time for the protest. Police always complain that we should approach them 10 days in advance, he said. Cockroach Janta Party activists visited Parliament Street Police Station on Monday to seek a date.

Article Title: Poland deploys 20,000 cops in schools, inspects 80k educational institutions amid rising youth violence
Article Text:
Ambulances stand outside a TEB Edukacja post-secondary school building following a knife attack on Minska Street in Warsaw, Poland, October 10, 2026.

Around 20,000 police officers are being deployed to schools across Poland on Monday after Prime Minister Donald Tusk pledged to tackle what he described as growing violence among young people.The deployment aims to strengthen security at schools following three recent stabbings within four days, Reuters reported.On Monday, police said they had inspected around 80,000 educational institutions and detained 135 people since Friday.Tusk, who chaired a crisis meeting on Sunday, said the glorification of violence in certain corners of the internet was having a harmful impact on young people."We have observed a rise in the fascination with violence, both in Poland and worldwide... we are witnessing a grim trend of violence," Tusk said, adding that content promoting Nazi ideology and a "cult of strength", along with violent computer games, were major contributing factors.In one case, police said a boy had created a model of his school in the Roblox game and simulated attacks on students. He was found in possession of a firearm, ammunition and knives.However, authorities dismissed rumours that the violent incidents were connected to an online challenge or an organised group.Reuters reported.On Thursday, a 15-year-old former pupil wearing a helmet-mounted camera killed a caretaker and injured two teachers at a primary school in Leszczydol-Nowiny, north-east of Warsaw.On Wednesday, a 19-year-old injured 10 people, including himself, at a school in Ostroleka, north of the capital.The most recent attack took place on Saturday, when three people were injured at a further education college in Warsaw. It was Poland's third stabbing attack at an educational institution in four days.Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said a "clear message" was needed."There will be no tolerance for any attacks on Polish children, nor for the descent of public life into anarchy," Kierwinski told state news channel TVP Info.
Article Summary: 20,000 police officers are being deployed to schools across Poland on Monday. Prime Minister Donald Tusk pledged to tackle growing violence among young people. Deployment aims to strengthen security at schools following three recent stabbings within four days. Police said they had inspected around 80,000 educational institutions and detained 135 people since Friday.
